```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(haven)
library(knitr)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

teal <- "#245E52"
ink  <- "#233C38"
loc_pal <- c("Headquarters area" = "#245E52", "Elsewhere" = "#93B6A7")

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15, base_family = "sans") +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title.position = "plot",
          axis.text  = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"),
          legend.text = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold"))
)

efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")
d <- zap_labels(efcu) |>
  mutate(
    q12 = na_if(q12, 3),                                   # "No answer" -> missing
    location = factor(q38, levels = 1:2, labels = c("Headquarters area", "Elsewhere"))
  )

fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "< .001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

item_labels <- c(
  Att_employee = "Att_employee: Employee proficiency (Q3–Q6)",
  q3  = "Q3: Employees are courteous",
  q4  = "Q4: Employees are helpful",
  q5  = "Q5: Employees are professional",
  q6  = "Q6: Employees are available",
  q9_r  = "Q9r: Statement frequency",
  q10_r = "Q10r: Statement accuracy",
  q31 = "Q31: Personnel keep info confidential",
  q32 = "Q32: Prompt in processing loans",
  q33 = "Q33: Services meet members' needs",
  q34 = "Q34: Loan applications simple",
  Q37_r = "Q37r: Overall management & operation"
)

# One-sample t-test row
one_t <- function(var, mu = 3) {
  x  <- na.omit(d[[var]])
  tt <- t.test(x, mu = mu)
  tibble(Item = item_labels[[var]], n = length(x), Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x),
         `Test value` = mu, t = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter),
         p = fmt_p(tt$p.value))
}

# Independent-groups (Welch) t-test row by location
loc_t <- function(var) {
  tt <- t.test(as.formula(paste(var, "~ location")), data = d)
  g  <- d |> group_by(location) |>
    summarise(m = mean(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), s = sd(.data[[var]], na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble(Item = item_labels[[var]],
         `HQ M (SD)`        = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", g$m[1], g$s[1]),
         `Elsewhere M (SD)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", g$m[2], g$s[2]),
         Difference = g$m[1] - g$m[2],
         t  = unname(tt$statistic), df = unname(tt$parameter),
         p  = fmt_p(tt$p.value), p_raw = tt$p.value)
}
```

## About this report

I used the cleaned Case 31 data from **128 members** to examine employee proficiency (R3), operational effectiveness (R6), and differences by location (R4). The sample includes 57 members in the headquarters area and 71 elsewhere.

Q3–Q6 support the employee proficiency index, **Att_employee** (α = .87). Q31–Q34 have lower reliability (α = .47), so I report them separately. Valid sample sizes vary where responses are missing.

The findings are summarized below, with expandable R code and supporting results. Tests use α = .05. Higher values indicate more favorable ratings on the rating items; statement frequency is interpreted through its response categories.

## R3: Attitudes toward employee proficiency

### R3: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3-freq
#| tbl-cap: "Employee proficiency items: % disagree, neutral and agree"
agree_split <- function(var) {
  x <- na.omit(d[[var]])
  tibble(Item = item_labels[[var]], n = length(x),
         `% disagree (1–2)` = 100 * mean(x <= 2),
         `% uncertain (3)`  = 100 * mean(x == 3),
         `% agree (4–5)`    = 100 * mean(x >= 4),
         Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x), Median = median(x))
}
map_dfr(c("q3", "q4", "q5", "q6"), agree_split) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-r3
#| fig-cap: "Mean agreement with each employee proficiency statement (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree)"
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-width: 9
d |>
  summarise(across(c(q3, q4, q5, q6), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "mean") |>
  mutate(label = c("Courteous", "Helpful", "Professional", "Available"),
         label = fct_reorder(label, mean)) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, label)) +
  geom_col(fill = teal, width = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", color = "#9a9a9a") +
  annotate("text", x = 3, y = 4.45, label = "Neutral", hjust = -0.1, color = "#6b6b6b", size = 4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mean)), hjust = -0.2, color = ink, fontface = "bold", size = 5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 5), breaks = 1:5, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Mean agreement", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### R3: One-sample t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r3
#| tbl-cap: "Employee proficiency: one-sample t-tests against the scale midpoint (3 = uncertain)"
map_dfr(c("Att_employee", "q3", "q4", "q5", "q6"), one_t) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

### R3: Findings

Members rated employees positively. The proficiency index averaged **4.21 out of 5**, above the neutral midpoint (*p* < .001; @tbl-r3).

Courtesy (4.35) and helpfulness (4.31) received the highest ratings. Professionalism and availability averaged 4.08. Availability showed the widest variation (*SD* = 0.79), making it a useful area for follow-up rather than evidence of a specific staffing problem.

## R6: Operational effectiveness

### R6: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Interval items: % favorable and descriptive statistics"
fav <- function(var, cut) {
  x <- na.omit(d[[var]])
  tibble(Item = item_labels[[var]], n = length(x),
         `% favorable` = 100 * mean(x >= cut),
         Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x), Median = median(x))
}
bind_rows(fav("q10_r", 3), fav("q31", 4), fav("q32", 4), fav("q33", 4),
          fav("q34", 4), fav("Q37_r", 4)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

*Favorable responses follow the thresholds in the code: Q10r ≥ 3, Q37r ≥ 4, and Q31–Q34 ≥ 4. Categorical responses are summarized in @tbl-r6-cat.*

```{r}
#| label: fig-r6
#| fig-cap: "Share of members giving a favorable answer on each operational item"
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 10
r6_fav <- tibble(
  item = c("Statements easy to understand (Q11)", "Statement accuracy good+ (Q10)",
           "Overall rating good+ (Q37)", "Info kept confidential (Q31)",
           "Statement frequency about right (Q9)", "Info kept confidential, yes/no (Q12)",
           "Prompt loan processing (Q32)", "Services meet needs (Q33)",
           "Loan applications simple (Q34)"),
  pct = c(100 * mean(d$q11 == 1), 100 * mean(d$q10_r >= 3),
          100 * mean(d$Q37_r >= 4, na.rm = TRUE), 100 * mean(d$q31 >= 4),
          100 * mean(d$q9 == 3), 100 * mean(d$q12 == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
          100 * mean(d$q32 >= 4), 100 * mean(d$q33 >= 4), 100 * mean(d$q34 >= 4))
) |>
  mutate(item = fct_reorder(item, pct))

ggplot(r6_fav, aes(pct, item)) +
  geom_col(fill = teal, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct)), hjust = -0.15, color = ink,
            fontface = "bold", size = 4.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 110), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                     labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "% of members with a favorable answer", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### R6: Chi-square goodness-of-fit test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-cat
#| tbl-cap: "Frequency and yes/no items: frequencies and chi-square goodness-of-fit tests"
gof <- function(var, labels, item) {
  tab <- table(factor(d[[var]], levels = names(labels)))
  tab <- tab[tab > 0]
  ct  <- chisq.test(tab)
  tibble(Item = item, Response = unname(labels[names(tab)]), n = as.integer(tab),
         Percent = 100 * as.integer(tab) / sum(tab),
         `Chi-square` = c(unname(ct$statistic), rep(NA, length(tab) - 1)),
         df = c(unname(ct$parameter), rep(NA, length(tab) - 1)),
         p  = c(fmt_p(ct$p.value), rep("", length(tab) - 1)))
}
bind_rows(
  gof("q9",  c("1" = "Too often", "2" = "Very often", "3" = "About right",
               "4" = "Not often enough", "5" = "Never"), "Q9: Statement frequency"),
  gof("q11", c("1" = "Yes", "2" = "No"), "Q11: Statements easy to understand"),
  gof("q12", c("1" = "Yes", "2" = "No"), "Q12: Account info kept confidential")
) |> kable(digits = 1)
```

### R6: One-sample t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r6-int
#| tbl-cap: "Interval items: one-sample t-tests against the scale midpoint (2.5 for the 4-point Q10r, 3 otherwise)"
bind_rows(
  one_t("q10_r", mu = 2.5),
  one_t("q31"), one_t("q32"), one_t("q33"), one_t("q34"),
  one_t("Q37_r")
) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

### R6: Findings

Overall, **84% of valid respondents rated management and operations good or excellent**. Statements were generally viewed as clear and accurate: 98% found them easy to understand, and accuracy averaged 3.47 out of 4.

About 23% said statements did not arrive often enough. On privacy, 78% agreed that staff kept information confidential, while 30% answered “no” to the separate yes/no question. These questions use different wording and response formats, so the percentages should be interpreted separately.

Loan processing (3.72), services meeting needs (3.59), and application simplicity (3.46) were rated above the neutral midpoint. Application simplicity received the lowest average rating. Reviewing statement preferences, privacy communication, and loan forms could help identify practical improvements.

## R4: Headquarters area vs. elsewhere

### R4a: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a-desc
#| tbl-cap: "Employee proficiency by location: % agree and means"
d |>
  group_by(Location = location) |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            `% agree (Att ≥ 4)` = 100 * mean(Att_employee >= 4),
            `Att_employee M` = mean(Att_employee), SD = sd(Att_employee),
            Q3 = mean(q3), Q4 = mean(q4), Q5 = mean(q5), Q6 = mean(q6)) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

### R4a: Independent-samples t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4a
#| tbl-cap: "Employee proficiency by location: independent-groups (Welch) t-tests"
map_dfr(c("Att_employee", "q3", "q4", "q5", "q6"), loc_t) |>
  select(-p_raw) |>
  kable(digits = 2)
```

### R4a: Findings

Employee proficiency averaged **4.28 in the headquarters area and 4.14 elsewhere**. The difference was not statistically significant (*p* = .196; @tbl-r4a). The individual employee items also showed no statistically significant differences.

The sample provides limited evidence of a location difference; it does not establish that members have identical service experiences.

### R4b: Descriptive statistics (cross-tabulation)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b
#| tbl-cap: "Awareness of services by location: % unaware and % who have used each service"
services <- c(
  q13_r = "Regular share accounts", q14_r = "Special subaccounts",
  q15_r = "Christmas club accounts", q16_r = "IRAs",
  q17_r = "MasterCard credit card", q18_r = "Signature loans",
  q19_r = "New car loans", q20_r = "Late model car loans",
  q21_r = "Older model car loans", q22_r = "Household goods loans",
  q23_r = "Recreational loans", q24_r = "Share collateralized loans",
  q25_r = "IRA loans", q26_r = "Line of credit loans"
)
r4b <- map_dfr(names(services), function(v) {
  tab <- table(d$location, factor(d[[v]], levels = 1:3))
  tab <- tab[, colSums(tab) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  ct  <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab))
  hq  <- d[[v]][d$q38 == 1]; el <- d[[v]][d$q38 == 2]
  tibble(Service = services[[v]],
         `HQ % unaware` = 100 * mean(hq == 1), `Else % unaware` = 100 * mean(el == 1),
         `HQ % used`    = 100 * mean(hq == 3), `Else % used`    = 100 * mean(el == 3),
         `Chi-square` = unname(ct$statistic), df = unname(ct$parameter),
         p = fmt_p(ct$p.value), `Fisher p` = fmt_p(fisher.test(tab)$p.value))
})
r4b |> select(Service:`Else % used`) |> kable(digits = 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-r4b
#| fig-cap: "Percent of members UNAWARE of each service, headquarters area vs. elsewhere"
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
r4b |>
  select(Service, `Headquarters area` = `HQ % unaware`, Elsewhere = `Else % unaware`) |>
  pivot_longer(-Service, names_to = "location", values_to = "pct") |>
  mutate(location = factor(location, levels = names(loc_pal)),
         Service = fct_reorder(Service, pct, .fun = mean)) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct, Service)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Service), color = "#c9c9c4", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(color = location), size = 4.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = loc_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 75), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "% unaware of the service", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### R4b: Chi-square test of independence

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4b-chi
#| tbl-cap: "Awareness by location: chi-square tests of independence (Fisher's exact p shown because some expected counts are below 5)"
r4b |> select(Service, `Chi-square`, df, p, `Fisher p`) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

### R4b: Findings

None of the 14 services showed a statistically significant association between location and awareness/use category (all chi-square *p* ≥ .15). Fisher’s exact tests led to the same conclusion.

The largest observed gap in unawareness was for MasterCard: **18% in the headquarters area versus 7% elsewhere**. Unawareness was high in both locations for IRA loans and share-collateralized loans.

These results support considering outreach across the membership. They do not show whether a particular campaign would improve awareness.

### R4c: Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| label: fig-r4c
#| fig-cap: "Mean ratings by location. Q34 has an unadjusted p = .025"
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-width: 10
plot_items <- c("Att_employee", "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "Q37_r")
short <- c(Att_employee = "Employee proficiency", q31 = "Q31 Confidentiality",
           q32 = "Q32 Prompt loans", q33 = "Q33 Meets needs",
           q34 = "Q34 Simple applications", Q37_r = "Q37r Overall rating")
d |>
  select(location, all_of(plot_items)) |>
  pivot_longer(-location, names_to = "item", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(item, location) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(item = factor(short[item], levels = rev(short[plot_items]))) |>
  ggplot(aes(mean, item)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = item), color = "#c9c9c4", linewidth = 2) +
  geom_point(aes(color = location), size = 5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = loc_pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(3, 4.5)) +
  labs(x = "Mean rating (1–5)", y = NULL, color = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### R4c: Independent-samples t-test

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-int
#| tbl-cap: "Operational effectiveness by location: independent-groups (Welch) t-tests"
r4c <- map_dfr(c("q9_r", "q10_r", "q31", "q32", "q33", "q34", "Q37_r"), loc_t)
r4c |> select(-p_raw) |> kable(digits = 2)
```

### R4c: Chi-square test of independence

```{r}
#| label: tbl-r4c-cat
#| tbl-cap: "Yes/no items by location: chi-square tests of independence"
map_dfr(c(q11 = "Q11: Statements easy to understand", q12 = "Q12: Account info kept confidential") |>
          imap(\(lab, v) list(v = v, lab = lab)), function(x) {
  tab <- table(d$location, d[[x$v]])
  ct  <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))
  tibble(Item = x$lab,
         `HQ % yes`   = 100 * tab[1, 1] / sum(tab[1, ]),
         `Else % yes` = 100 * tab[2, 1] / sum(tab[2, ]),
         `Chi-square` = unname(ct$statistic), df = unname(ct$parameter),
         p = fmt_p(ct$p.value), `Fisher p` = fmt_p(fisher.test(tab)$p.value))
}) |> kable(digits = 1)
```



### R4c: Findings

Headquarters-area members rated loan application simplicity lower: **3.28 versus 3.61**, with an unadjusted *p* = .025 (@tbl-r4c-int). Because several items were tested, this is an exploratory finding that needs caution.

The other tested rating items showed no statistically significant location differences. The yes/no items also showed no statistically significant differences.

Reviewing the application process may be useful, but the survey does not explain the observed gap or establish that headquarters-area members were more frustrated.


## Summary

| Question | Main finding | Practical takeaway |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **R3: Employees** | Proficiency averaged **4.21/5** | Maintain positive staff service; explore availability |
| **R6: Operations** | **84%** rated operations good or excellent | Review statement preferences, privacy communication, and loan forms |
| **R4a: Employee ratings by location** | No statistically significant difference (*p* = .196) | Avoid assuming the groups have identical experiences |
| **R4b: Awareness by location** | No statistically significant associations across 14 services | Consider outreach across the membership |
| **R4c: Operations by location** | Q34 differed at unadjusted *p* = .025 | Treat the result as exploratory |

## Reflection

This analysis helped me connect each research question to a suitable test. I also learned to separate a small observed difference from a statistically significant result. For EFCU, the useful next step is to review the lower-rated areas and ask members what would improve their experience.
